question: Do interval-wise comparisons of parameters and empirical neural tangent kernels reveal a reproducible transition from chaotic exploration to constrained but still nonlinear refinement during neural-network training?

key_findings.claim: An extremely small parameter perturbation has a large long-run effect when injected before a trajectory inflection point and a much smaller effect when injected afterward.
key_findings.evidence: For VGG-16 and ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10, paired runs differing by an L0-normalized perturbation of 1e-7 separate in parameter direction, develop an interpolation loss barrier, and disagree on predictions when the perturbation is early. These measures fall sharply for perturbations after the empirically identified inflection point.

key_findings.claim: After the transition, empirical NTK matrices continue moving but remain within a narrow angular region relative to late reference kernels.
key_findings.evidence: Pairwise kernel-distance heatmaps and distances to varying reference times show rapid early movement followed by a confined region. The authors call this the cone effect and distinguish it from a frozen-kernel lazy regime because adjacent kernels still change.

key_findings.claim: Late training inside the cone retains a measurable advantage over switching to a linearized model, so stability does not imply fully lazy dynamics.
key_findings.evidence: Runs switched from standard training to a local linearization increasingly underperform continued nonlinear training in test accuracy and loss when the switch occurs after roughly 2,000 iterations. The comparison supports continued feature evolution, although it does not identify the causal mechanism of the cone.

method.core_idea: Compare network states across time intervals rather than summarize each checkpoint independently, using perturbation response and angular empirical-NTK distance.
method.mechanism: The study samples training checkpoints, locates a directional inflection, forks otherwise identical optimization runs with tiny parameter perturbations, and measures later parameter dissimilarity, loss barriers, and prediction disagreement. It separately tracks cosine distance among empirical NTK matrices and tests late nonlinear value by switching to linearized training.
assumptions: Angular distances between parameters and eNTKs capture meaningful dynamical regimes.
Numerically tiny injected perturbations isolate sensitivity to initial conditions rather than implementation nondeterminism.
CIFAR architectures and schedules are representative enough to motivate a broader two-phase hypothesis.

techniques.role: Measures movement and confinement between pairs of empirical NTKs over training.
Tests when tiny parameter changes alter the eventual basin and predictions.
Separates a constrained nonlinear regime from frozen-kernel lazy training.

evaluations.setting: VGG-16 and ResNet-20 trained on CIFAR-10 under multiple settings
evaluations.metric: parameter cosine distance, interpolation loss barrier, prediction disagreement, and eNTK cosine distance
evaluations.result: All measures show a marked early-to-late transition; perturbations before the inflection produce substantially greater separation than perturbations after it.
evaluations.baseline: Unperturbed paired training and perturbations injected at later checkpoints.

evaluations.metric: test accuracy and test loss at the common final iteration
evaluations.result: Later switches still trail continued standard training, with the gap becoming pronounced after about 2,000 iterations.
evaluations.baseline: Continued nonlinear training and locally linearized continuation.

limitations: Author-stated: the paper is primarily empirical and does not derive why the transition or cone occurs.
Author-stated: evaluation is concentrated on standard vision architectures and CIFAR-scale data.
Reviewer inference: the chosen inflection and angular metrics can make a gradual change look phase-like without finite-size scaling or a formal order parameter.
Reviewer inference: proximity of transition times across metrics is correlational and does not establish a single mechanism.
failure_modes: The apparent transition moves or disappears under different normalization, optimizer, batch order, or perturbation direction.
Full empirical-NTK estimation on a sample subset misses function-space directions important to generalization.
High-dimensional angular concentration produces a visually narrow cone without strong predictive meaning.
reusable_insights: Perturb-at-checkpoint experiments provide an operational test of when optimization becomes stable.
A slowly changing kernel and a frozen kernel are different hypotheses and should be benchmarked separately.
Training-regime claims benefit from interval matrices that expose relations among all checkpoint pairs.
open_questions: Which optimizer, architecture, data, and scale variables control the transition time and cone angle?
Can a prospective metric detect the transition online and improve schedules or checkpoint allocation?
Is the late cone causally linked to generalization, basin connectivity, or representation stabilization?

competitive_landscape.title: Deep learning versus kernel learning: an empirical study of loss landscape geometry and the time evolution of the Neural Tangent Kernel
competitive_landscape.difference: Fort et al. report a rapid chaotic transient followed by stable, approximately constant-velocity NTK evolution. This paper adds controlled checkpoint perturbations and characterizes the late kernels as angularly confined but still nonlinear.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Cone Effect in the Learning Dynamics
competitive_landscape.difference: The companion paper introduces the empirical eNTK cone and late-linearization comparison. The present paper packages that result with the new chaos-effect perturbation experiment to argue for one two-phase structural account.

competitive_landscape.title: Dissecting the Effects of SGD Noise in Distinct Regimes of Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: That work separates SGD-noise effects across optimization regimes and studies their implicit regularization. This paper instead diagnoses regime boundaries through perturbation amplification and eNTK geometry without attributing them primarily to SGD noise.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after comparison: the new contribution is the chaos-effect perturbation assay and its alignment with an eNTK cone transition; the cone result itself substantially overlaps the authors' earlier companion paper. The combined evidence is a useful phenomenology, not yet a universal phase-transition theory.
reviewer_notes: Full text, plots, definitions, linearization control, related work, and limitations were reviewed. Competitors and the closely overlapping companion preprint were checked at primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
